newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal sets contract highs, soyoil ends up.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal sets contract highs, soyoil ends up.

text.p: Contract highs were set in nearby CBOT soymeal futures on Thursday and soyoil ended higher on surprisingly tight February soymeal stocks as reported by the U.S. Census Bureau, traders said.

"The February crush number was strong," said Allen Dever, analyst with Doane Agriculture Services. "The crush is running at a seasonally adjusted pace of 1.564 billion bushels. USDA put it at 1.42 billion. Clearly we're running at a pace we cannot sustain or we'll run out of soybeans."
Soymeal stocks were at 165,278 tons in the Census report, below expectations for 220,000 and 240,000 tons.
The report, along with recent news several ADM and Cargill Inc crushing plants would be down this summer, confirmed ideas that supplies were dwindling while demand held steady.
Contract highs were notched in the May, July, August and September contracts and the front months touched the $10 per ton upper limit before crushers sold late in the session.
Floor sources cited reports cash soymeal basis levels in Brazil had fallen.
Soymeal closed $6.10 to $1.80 per ton higher with May up $6.10 at $280.30 a ton. Soyoil closed 0.16 to 0.08 cent per lb higher with May up 0.08 at 24.77.
The new contract high for the May is $284.20 per ton, topping the previous high of $278.00 set on March 11. That was also the highest level for a spot contract since August 1988.
"Export sales were good and meal stocks were low in the crush and we still have the threat of flooding this spring," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter. "There was fund buying and a lack of offers."
Reports of the drop in Brazilian basis levels trimmed gains late. Crushers were said to be noted sellers.
"The Brazilian nearby meal basis is breaking," said Steve Bruce of E.D. and F. Man International.

On the day, Goldenberg-Hehmeyer and Refco Inc each bought at least 500 lots May soymeal. Smith Barney sold 200 May and 300 July while ING Futures sold 300 May. Cargill Inc, Continental Grain, FCC and Produce Grain were said to be buyers in morning trade.
Floor sources said Cargill, ADM and Bunge were sellers late.
In soyoil, Cargill Inc bought 600 May and 200 July early, Term Commodities bought 400 May and 100 July. Rosenthal Collins bought 800 May and FIMAT Futures bought 400 May.
Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 30,000 lots, compared with Wednesday's actual volume of 20,546 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 21,000 lots, against 13,167 lots on Wednesday.
